newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela cool to Colombia rebels' mediation offer.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela cool to Colombia rebels' mediation offer.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera said Thursday that mediation suggested by Colombian guerrillas to free 60 soldiers they have held prisoner for six months could only take place if the Colombian government backed it.
In a letter to Caldera made public on Wednesday, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) said he would be well-placed to end the standoff.
In a statement, the Miraflores presidential palace replied: "The suitability of any mediation depends on how pertinent...and propitious...the Colombian government sees it (to be)."
The Marxist FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, took the 60 soldiers prisoner Aug. 30 after an attack on a remote military base in Colombia's southern Putumayo jungle.
In its letter, dated Jan. 22, the FARC told Caldera the soldiers would be freed if Colombian President Ernesto Samper ordered the army's withdrawal from areas in the south of the country.
